elastic

/ih-LAS-tik/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Elastic means able to spring back to its original shape after being stretched or compressed.

The elastic waistband stretched to fit and then snapped right back to its original size.

Example

The trampoline's surface is elastic; it dips deep under a jumper's weight and instantly springs flat again the moment the jumper lifts off.

The trampoline stretches under pressure and returns to its original shape as soon as the pressure is gone. That snap-back behavior is what makes a material elastic.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

stretchy: Stretchy means able to be pulled longer easily — stretchy fabric gives when you tug it. That covers only half of what elastic means: an elastic material both stretches and then springs back to its original shape, while a stretchy one may simply stay stretched out.

springy: Springy describes a surface that pushes back the instant it is pressed or compressed, like a trampoline or a firm mattress. It is about rebound from squeezing. Elastic covers the fuller cycle: being stretched or compressed and then returning to the exact original shape afterward.

rubbery: Rubbery means having the feel and give of rubber — bendable, slightly stretchy, a little bouncy. It names a texture. Elastic names a precise behavior: returning to the original shape after being stretched or compressed. Something can feel rubbery yet sag; elastic things snap back.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

rigid: unable to bend

brittle: snapping instead of bending

Where it sits · how forcefully it returns to shape

flexible → elastic → spring-loaded

flexible vs. elastic: A flexible material simply bends without breaking, while an elastic one pulls itself back to its original shape.

spring-loaded vs. elastic: An elastic band eases back into shape, but a spring-loaded latch snaps back with sudden force.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — elast: to drive or set in motion (from Greek elaunein)

Suffix — -ic: having characteristics of

Put it together: The Greek root elast- means to drive or set in motion, and -ic means having that quality, so an elastic material is one that drives itself back into shape after being stretched.

Use the root in a new word: elasticity: Engineers measured the elasticity of the new cable before approving it for the bridge.

Word Building

Word Choice

Neutral / everyday

Used for physical materials like waistbands, rubber, and springs, and in an extended sense for arrangements that can stretch, like an elastic deadline or elastic demand in economics. Keep it separate from resilience, which describes a person's or system's capacity to recover, not a material's stretchiness.
